findings.message: The path exemption is still open to one slash-bearing secret shape. A value that starts with `/` counts as path-shaped, and the check then looks for a 52+ character run in each `/`-split segment on its own. A base64 key that begins with `/` and has internal `/` characters passes as a path once every segment is under 52 characters, even though the whole value is a long token. Use the path exemption only when the value has a path-like structure, for example it has a path-looking prefix such as /home, /Users, /etc, /var or /tmp, or at least one segment contains `.` or `-` as a filename. Alternatively, apply the whole-value `[A-Za-z0-9+/_-]{52,}` test when the value has no `.` or `-` segment separators. Add a variant row for a leading-slash base64 secret.
findings.scenario: `vault: /Ab1cdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234/ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ012345` (about 70 characters, a base64-style key whose first character is `/`) matches the path-shaped regex. Both segments are under 52 characters, so looks_secret returns 1 and the secret is accepted into config.

findings.message: The new skip branch `[[ -n "$k" && -n "$z" ]]` is exercised only when both names are absent (the `nofile` case). The one-name-resolved case is untested: only the kube name found, or only the azure name found, from the pipeline file or from the environment. The branch also drops the old per-name defaults, so a pipeline file that declares only one of the two variables now skips permanently. Add table rows for each single-name case. Also fix the skip message, which names `FLEET_PIPELINE_FILE` or the default path and may not be the file `pipeline_var` actually read when `fleet.pipeline_file` is set.
findings.scenario: The pipeline YAML declares only `fleetKubeConnection`, and `FLEET_AZURE_CONNECTION` is unset. check_connections prints `skip service-connections: no connection names...` and returns 2. No test covers this, and it is a behaviour change from the earlier default `specclaw-fleet-azure`.
